acceptance_criteria: Given/When/Then statements, each independently testable
_schema.cycle_done: cycle number that shipped it, or null

_notes: Product has no UI. 'backend' scope = plugin (C2), validation tooling (C1), installers (C5) and key provisioning (C6), all living under backend/. 'frontend' is false for every item.
FR-11: the shipped plugin must be ONE TypeScript file with zero runtime npm dependencies. Dev-only tooling (test runner, type-checker) is allowed.
External systems (Azure DevOps, az CLI, Bifrost, Kilo) are never called for real in tests; they are faked/mocked.

items.title: Project skeleton & CI
items.description: Architect picks the stack (expected: TypeScript, zero runtime deps, built-in or dev-only test runner) and records it in ADR-0001, including the supported Kilo version range and the layout under backend/ (plugin single file, validation tooling, installers, provisioning). Senior BE creates a minimal plugin stub and one smoke test. CI releaser wires scripts/ci.sh and GitHub Actions to a green pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean checkout, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` is run, Then it exits 0 and the output shows the backend package's type-check and test steps were executed (not the 'no packages yet' path).

Given the repository, When docs/architecture/ADR-0001-tech-stack.md is read by an automated check, Then the file exists and contains sections for language/runtime, test runner, supported Kilo version range, and the zero-runtime-dependency single-file plugin constraint (FR-11).

Given the backend package, When the test suite runs, Then a smoke test imports the single plugin source file (e.g. backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts) and asserts it exports a plugin function that, when invoked with a minimal fake Kilo context, returns an object exposing a `config` hook.
Given backend/package.json, When an automated check inspects it, Then the `dependencies` field is absent or empty (only devDependencies are allowed).
Given a push or pull request to main, When the GitHub Actions CI workflow runs, Then it executes `bash scripts/ci.sh` (verifiable by a check that .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes scripts/ci.sh).
Given the plugin stub, When its `config` hook is invoked with a config object, Then it resolves without throwing and leaves the object unchanged (no-op until F-features land).

items.title: Plugin: JSONC parser
items.description: FR-4 / AC-5. Pure, exported function (e.g. `parseJsonc(text: string): unknown`) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Strips line/block comments and trailing commas outside strings, then JSON.parse. Zero runtime deps (FR-11). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006).
acceptance_criteria: Given JSONC with `//` line comments and `/* */` block comments (including a multi-line block comment and a comment at end of file without trailing newline), When parsed, Then the result deep-equals the same document without comments.
Given JSONC with trailing commas in objects and arrays (including nested and with whitespace/comments between the comma and the closing bracket), When parsed, Then it parses to the expected object.
Given string values containing `https://host/path`, `/* not a comment */` and a literal `,}` sequence, When parsed, Then each string value is preserved exactly.

Given strings containing escaped quotes (`\"`) and escaped backslashes (a string ending in an escaped backslash, e.g. JSON source `"C:\\"`) followed by `//`, When parsed, Then string boundaries are respected and content is preserved.

Given invalid JSONC (unterminated string, unterminated block comment, or malformed JSON), When parsed, Then an Error with a descriptive message is thrown and the input text is not echoed in full in the message.

Given the Appendix A example from VISION.md, When parsed, Then provider.bifrost.options.baseURL equals `https://bifrost.yourcompany.internal/v1` and provider.bifrost.models has keys `azure/gpt-5` and `azure/gpt-5-mini`.
Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0 and backend/package.json still has no runtime `dependencies`.

items.title: Plugin: {env:} and {file:} placeholder resolution
items.description: FR-5 / AC-8. Pure helper exposed as `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` (ADR-0002 seam) inside the single plugin file backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts. Recursively resolves `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` placeholders in the parsed shared config and returns `{ value, unresolved }` where `unresolved` is a list of placeholder names (never values). Environment, home directory and file reader are injectable for tests (defaults: process.env, os.homedir(), fs.readFileSync). Not yet wired into the config hook (F-006). Zero runtime deps (FR-11).
acceptance_criteria: Given `{"x": "{env:SET_VAR}"}` and an injected env with SET_VAR=abc, When `__internals.resolvePlaceholders` runs, Then result.value.x equals `abc` and result.unresolved is empty.

Given `{"x": "{env:MISSING}", "y": 1}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then key x is absent from result.value (not present as undefined/empty), y equals 1, and result.unresolved contains exactly `env:MISSING`.
Given `{"x": "pre-{env:MISSING}-post"}` with MISSING unset, When resolved, Then x equals `pre--post` and result.unresolved contains `env:MISSING`.

Given `{"x": "{file:~/secret.txt}"}` and secret.txt containing `  s3cret\n` under an injected fake home directory, When resolved, Then x equals `s3cret` (trimmed) and the file read targeted `<home>/secret.txt` (`~/` expanded).

Given `{file:...}` that cannot be read (missing path, a directory, or a reader that throws with the file contents in its error message), When resolved, Then the key is dropped, result.unresolved contains `file:<path as written>`, and no returned or thrown value contains the file contents or the reader's error text.

Given placeholders nested in objects and arrays (e.g. `{"a":{"b":["{env:SET_VAR}","{env:MISSING}","keep"]}}`), When resolved, Then nested values follow the same rules, an array element that is only an unresolved placeholder is removed from the array (giving `["abc","keep"]`), and non-string values (numbers, booleans, null) and strings without placeholders are returned unchanged.

Given any input object, When resolved, Then the input object is not mutated, own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` in the input do not pollute Object.prototype, and a string containing multiple placeholders (`{env:A}/{env:B}`) resolves each one.

Given the plugin package after the change, When `bash scripts/ci.sh` (including the FR-11 lint) runs, Then it exits 0, backend/package.json has no runtime `dependencies`, and the only new export surface is the `resolvePlaceholders` key on `__internals`.

items.title: Plugin: in-place merge with defaults/enforce modes
items.description: FR-6 / AC-6 / AC-7. Deep merge of shared config into Kilo's resolved config object, mutating it in place.
acceptance_criteria: Given local and shared both set `model` differently, When merged in `defaults` mode, Then the local value is kept.
Given local and shared both set `model` differently, When merged in `enforce` mode, Then the shared value is kept.
Given local `provider.bifrost.options.apiKey` and a shared provider.bifrost block, When merged in either mode, Then apiKey is unchanged.
Given keys present locally but absent from the shared file, When merged, Then those keys are unchanged.
Given the shared file contains `$schema` and `plugin`, When merged, Then the local `$schema` and `plugin` values are unchanged.
Given a config object reference, When merged, Then the same object reference is mutated (not replaced) and nested objects are deep-merged.

Given overlay/remote config containing own keys `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`, When merged, Then those keys are skipped or own-defined and Object.prototype is not polluted (regression test).

items.title: Plugin: settings resolution (options, env, defaults)
items.description: FR-1 / FR-8. Resolve org, project, repo, path, branch, mode, pat, timeoutMs.
acceptance_criteria: Given plugin options set `org`, When settings resolve, Then options win over KILO_AZDO_ORG.
Given no option but KILO_AZDO_BRANCH=dev, When settings resolve, Then branch equals `dev`.
Given neither options nor env, When settings resolve, Then built-in defaults apply (path `/kilo.jsonc`, branch `main`, mode `defaults`, timeoutMs 5000).
Given an invalid mode value, When settings resolve, Then mode falls back to `defaults` and a warning is logged.
Given a non-numeric or non-positive timeoutMs, When settings resolve, Then 5000 is used.

items.title: Plugin: Azure DevOps fetch and authentication
items.description: FR-2 / FR-3 / FR-8. Fetch via Git Items API using injected fetch and injected `az` runner for testability.
acceptance_criteria: Given settings, When fetching, Then the request URL targets `https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/git/repositories/{repo}/items` with path, versionDescriptor.version=branch, versionDescriptor.versionType=branch, includeContent=true, api-version=7.1 (all URL-encoded).
Given a `pat` option, When fetching, Then the Authorization header is `Basic base64(':' + pat)`.
Given no pat option but AZDO_PAT or AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT set, When fetching, Then that PAT is used with Basic auth (AZDO_PAT preferred).
Given no PAT anywhere, When fetching, Then the faked `az account get-access-token --resource 499b84ac-1321-427f-aa17-267ca6975798` token is used as `Bearer`.
Given a server that does not respond within timeoutMs, When fetching, Then the fetch is aborted and a timeout error is returned.
Given a non-2xx response, When fetching, Then an error including the HTTP status (but no token) is returned.
Given a remote config response larger than a fixed cap (e.g. 1 MiB), When fetched, Then it is rejected before parseJsonc is called (parseJsonc memory is ~50x input size).

items.title: Plugin: cache, fallback, logging and never-crash wiring
items.description: FR-7 / FR-9 / FR-10 / AC-3 / AC-4 / AC-8 / AC-9. Wire the full startup sequence into the plugin's config hook.
acceptance_criteria: Given a successful fetch, When the config hook runs, Then the resolved config is written to `<home>/.cache/kilo-azdo/remote-config.json` and merged into the config.
Given the fetch fails and a cache exists, When the config hook runs, Then the cached config is merged and a warning is logged with service `azdo-remote-config` (AC-3).
Given the fetch fails and no cache exists, When the config hook runs, Then the config is unchanged and an error is logged (AC-4).
Given any internal exception (parse error, unwritable cache, logger failure), When the config hook runs, Then it does not throw (FR-10).
Given a run with a PAT, a bearer token and an `sk-bf-` key present, When all log calls are captured, Then none contains any of those secret values (AC-9).
Given `{env:MISSING}` in the shared file, When the hook runs, Then the log names `env:MISSING` and contains no value (AC-8).
Given a successful fetch on POSIX, When the cache file is written, Then its permissions are 0600 and the cache directory is created if missing (security follow-up, cycle 0002).

Given a Windows host where process.env lookups are case-insensitive, When {env:NAME} placeholders are resolved through the hook, Then behaviour is documented/tested (injected envs are case-sensitive; process.env is not).

items.title: Shared config repo: example kilo.jsonc and validation script
items.description: FR-12 / FR-13 / AC-13. Template content for C1 plus a zero-dependency validator CLI used by the PR pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Given the shipped example /kilo.jsonc, When validated, Then the validator exits 0.
Given a file containing an `apiKey` field at any depth, When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero and names the JSON path.
Given a file containing a string matching `sk-bf-`, When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero without printing the full secret.
Given a file with invalid JSONC, When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero with a parse error.
Given a file whose structure violates the vendored Kilo config schema subset (e.g. `provider` not an object), When validated, Then the validator exits non-zero.
Given a shared config containing a relative {file:} path, bare ~, ~user or UNC-style path, When validated, Then the validator warns that it will never resolve.

items.title: Shared config repo: Azure Pipelines PR gate and branch policy setup
items.description: FR-13 / FR-14. azure-pipelines.yml running the validator on PRs, and a script (az repos policy) that applies the main branch policy.
acceptance_criteria: Given azure-pipelines.yml, When parsed by a test, Then it triggers on PRs to main and runs the validator against kilo.jsonc and teams/*/kilo.jsonc.

Given the branch-policy script run in dry-run mode, When executed, Then it prints `az repos policy` commands for: minimum 1 reviewer, required platform-team reviewer group, and build validation on the pipeline.
Given the branch-policy script without required arguments, When executed, Then it exits non-zero with usage help.

items.title: Personal config template
items.description: FR-16 / FR-17. Template matching Appendix B.
acceptance_criteria: Given the template, When parsed, Then its top-level keys are only `$schema`, `plugin` and `provider`.
Given the template, When inspected, Then `plugin` has exactly one entry pointing at `./azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` with options org, project, repo, path, branch, mode.
Given the template, When inspected, Then `provider` contains only `bifrost.options.apiKey` with a placeholder value that does not match a real key pattern.
Given the template, When validated by the F-007 validator's secret check, Then no real `sk-bf-` secret is detected (placeholder only).

items.title: Bootstrap installer for macOS/Linux (install.sh)
items.description: FR-18..FR-23 / AC-12 / AC-14 for POSIX. Tests run with a temp HOME and faked az/curl.
acceptance_criteria: Given a temp HOME with no Kilo config, When install.sh runs, Then the plugin is at `~/.config/kilo/azdo/azdo-remote-config.ts` and the personal config is created from the template.
Given an existing personal config with other keys, When install.sh runs, Then only the plugin entry and apiKey are added/updated and other keys are preserved.
Given install.sh, When it runs, Then nothing is written to `~/.config/kilo/plugin/` (plugin loads exactly once, AC-12).
Given az missing and no PAT, When install.sh runs, Then it prints a clear fix and exits non-zero.
Given install.sh is run twice, When the config directory is diffed, Then the second run changed nothing except the plugin file (AC-14).
Given faked AzDO and Bifrost endpoints, When the smoke test step runs, Then it reports pass or fail for both checks without printing the key.

items.title: Bootstrap installer for Windows (install.ps1)
items.description: FR-18..FR-23 / AC-12 / AC-14 for Windows, behaviour parity with install.sh. Tests via Pester or pwsh where available; skipped with a clear message otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Given a temp USERPROFILE with no Kilo config, When install.ps1 runs, Then the plugin and personal config are created as with install.sh.
Given an existing personal config with other keys, When install.ps1 runs, Then other keys are preserved.
Given install.ps1, When it runs, Then nothing is written to the auto-loaded plugin directory.
Given az missing and no PAT, When install.ps1 runs, Then it prints a clear fix and exits non-zero.
Given install.ps1 is run twice, Then the second run changes nothing except the plugin file.

items.title: Key provisioning: create virtual key per engineer
items.description: FR-24 / FR-27. CLI calling Bifrost governance API (faked in tests).
acceptance_criteria: Given an email, budget, rate limit and model list, When `create` runs, Then one POST to the governance virtual-keys endpoint is made with name = email and those limits.

Given a successful create, When output and logs are captured, Then the key value is never printed to stdout/logs; it is written only to a per-engineer file with 0600 permissions (or delivered via a pluggable secure-channel hook).
Given a governance API error, When `create` runs, Then it exits non-zero with the HTTP status and no admin token in output.
Given the admin token, When the tool runs, Then it is read from an env var, never from a CLI argument or the shared repo.

items.title: Key provisioning: bulk CSV, list and disable (offboarding)
acceptance_criteria: Given a CSV of engineers where some already have keys, When `bulk` runs, Then keys are created only for engineers without one (no duplicates).
Given `bulk` is run twice with the same CSV, Then the second run creates nothing.
Given `list`, When run, Then it prints engineer names and key status without key values.
Given `disable alice@x`, When run, Then only alice's key is disabled and no other key is modified (AC-11).
Given `disable` for an unknown email, When run, Then it exits non-zero and modifies nothing.

items.title: End-to-end simulated startup test
items.description: AC-1 / AC-2 / AC-10 simulated: local fake AzDO + fake Bifrost servers exercise the whole plugin flow.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fake AzDO server serving a shared kilo.jsonc, When the plugin config hook runs, Then the resulting config lists the Bifrost models (AC-1, simulated).
Given the shared file changes on the fake server, When the hook runs again, Then the new value is in effect with no other change (AC-2).
Given the fake Bifrost enforces auth, When a request without a virtual key is made, Then it is rejected with 401 and the installer smoke test reports fail (AC-10, simulated).

items.title: Per-team config files support
items.description: FR-15. Example /teams/<team>/kilo.jsonc and validation coverage; plugin `path` option selects it.
acceptance_criteria: Given path `/teams/payments/kilo.jsonc`, When the plugin fetches, Then the request targets that path.
Given an example team file, When validated, Then the validator exits 0.
Given a team file with an apiKey, When the pipeline validator runs over teams/*, Then it fails.

items.title: User and operator documentation
items.description: Engineer setup guide, platform-team runbook (config change, key provisioning, offboarding), KILO_PURE caveat, supported Kilo version range, Phase 0 assumptions A1-A3 checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Given docs/, When an automated check runs, Then engineer setup, platform runbook and troubleshooting pages exist and link to each other.
Given the troubleshooting page, When checked, Then it mentions KILO_PURE=1, az login and the cache location.
Given all docs, When scanned for `sk-bf-` followed by real-looking key material, Then none is found.

items.title: Harden FR-11 lint against import evasions
items.description: Security/review: backend/tools/check-fr11.mjs regexes can be bypassed (template-literal or variable import(), createRequire, a "/*" string literal). Use ts.preProcessFile/AST, reject non-literal import() and createRequire, and add fixtures for these plus untested branches (export-from, bare import, missing/invalid package.json, missing plugin/, --root without value).
acceptance_criteria: Given a plugin file using import(`lodash`), import(variable), createRequire, or a "/*" string hiding an import, When check-fr11 runs, Then it exits 1.
Given fixtures for export-from, bare import, missing/invalid package.json, missing plugin/ and --root without a value, When tests run, Then each is covered and behaves as specified.

items.title: Release build step packaging the plugin file
items.description: Copy plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts to backend/dist/ so release.yml attaches it as an artefact; fits with the installer items.
acceptance_criteria: Given a release, When release.yml runs, Then backend/dist/azdo-remote-config.ts is attached and byte-identical to the source.

items.title: Escape raw BOM literal and lint invisible characters
items.description: backend/plugin/azdo-remote-config.ts:38 holds a raw U+FEFF in the BOM constant; replace with the "\ufeff" escape sequence (six ASCII characters) and add a CI check (e.g. in check-fr11 or a script) that flags invisible characters in source files. Optionally copy unchanged text runs by slice in parseJsonc to cut memory (security low finding, cycle 0003).
acceptance_criteria: Given the plugin source, When inspected, Then the BOM constant is written as the ASCII escape "\ufeff" and the file contains no raw U+FEFF.
Given a source file containing a raw invisible character, When the CI check runs, Then it exits non-zero.

items.title: CHANGELOG missing v0.1.0 (F-001) entry
items.description: state.json records v0.1.0 released in cycle 3 for F-001, but CHANGELOG.md only lists 0.0.1. CI releaser should backfill the [0.1.0] entry (can be done alongside the next release).
acceptance_criteria: Given CHANGELOG.md, When an automated check reads it, Then it has a `## [0.1.0]` section mentioning F-001 and the version in VERSION has a matching section.

items.title: Placeholder resolver test hardening
items.description: Review info findings on backend/test/plugin/placeholders.test.ts: the inherited-env-names test would pass without the own-property check; the 1 MiB cap is only tested at cap+1. Security info: also check length after reading to cover /proc pseudo-files reporting size 0.
acceptance_criteria: Given an env created via Object.create({INH:'x'}), When {env:INH} is resolved, Then it is unresolved (test fails if the own-property check is removed).
Given a file of exactly 1 MiB, When read with the default reader, Then it resolves; at 1 MiB + 1 it does not.
Given a reader result longer than the cap, When resolved, Then it is treated as unresolved.

items.title: Optional allowlist for {file:} and {env:} placeholders
items.description: Security finding 2 (accepted risk in cycle 0004): the shared config can read any env var or user-readable file. Add an optional allowlist/path-prefix limit configurable in settings to reduce exfiltration blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Given an allowlist of env names and path prefixes, When a placeholder outside it is resolved, Then it is unresolved and reported by name only.
Given no allowlist configured, When resolving, Then behaviour is unchanged (backwards compatible).
